question: What is the core idea of Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE)?
options: Iteratively merge the most frequent pair of adjacent symbols into a new token
Hash every word to a fixed integer
Use the Unicode block of each character as the token

question: Why does BPE handle out-of-vocabulary words gracefully?
options: Any word can be decomposed into a sequence of known subword pieces, down to single bytes
It silently replaces unknown words with <unk>
It memorizes every English word in advance

question: BPE is typically trained:
options: Once, on a large corpus, before model training begins
Never — modern models use character-level tokenization

question: Sort each token by what it represents in a typical BPE vocabulary.
explanation: Pieces beginning or ending with ## are merge fragments — they only appear glued to other pieces. Standalone strings without that marker are full vocabulary entries that map directly to a word.
